purpose: ROUND 31 sourcing receipt for the DOW-bromine litmus's cost-ranking lane. Historical figures are LABELLED HISTORICAL and recorded here, NEVER admitted to the modern USGS/Methanex commodity seeds (the R22 Los Fresnos discipline). Machine-readable companion to docs/research/DOW_BROMINE_COST_RANKING_CONTRACT_v0.1.md and experiments/dow_bromine_cost_probe.py.

theorem_1_modern_degeneracy.claim: A NaBr feedstock priced purely by contained-Br mass fraction from the SAME bromine benchmark q costs EXACTLY q per unit Br2 (p(NaBr)=q*M(Br)/M(NaBr); stoichiometry needs M(NaBr)/M(Br) NaBr per unit Br2; product = q). Any positive oxidant/process cost then makes brine STRICTLY > mined.
theorem_1_modern_degeneracy.verdict_scope: SCOPED NEGATIVE: 'no undercut is demonstrable from the sourced same-benchmark proxy'. NOT a claim that brine loses in reality -- real well-brine bromine (Smackover, Dead Sea) DOES undercut market Br2 via a nearly-free INDEPENDENT feedstock basis we cannot source today.
theorem_1_modern_degeneracy.certification_gate: An undercut is certifiable ONLY on a feedstock price that is BOTH independently sourced (not derived from the benchmark being undercut) AND separately observed/dated/labelled. The proxy fails this; an unsourced injected value fails it; a gate that opens on any handed-in value is not a gate (birdperson).
theorem_1_modern_degeneracy.source: docs/research/SOURCING_RECON_2026-09-07.md conditional cost obstruction (claim ledger: 'A same-benchmark Br-content-derived NaBr proxy can establish an undercut -> Refuted').

bromine_benchmark_q.basis: USGS import unit value, per kg contained Br, 2024 final (R16 seed)

chlorine_recon.basis: Los Fresnos approved municipal offer $1.24/lb one-ton cylinder = $2,480/2000lb; 0.45359237 kg/lb
chlorine_recon.status: LABELLED reconnaissance, NOT a committed default price (R22)

theorem_2_historical_undercut.claim: The sustained multi-year USGS US bromine unit value is an upper bound on the US brine-route marginal cost (industry produced+sold at it for years; whole-industry multi-year cross-subsidy implausible). Against the cartel's administered 49 c/lb: ~39% undercut at normal pre-war prices, >= ~80% against the war-survival cost ceiling.
theorem_2_historical_undercut.one_sidedness: ECONOMIC and DEFEASIBLE (a firm/industry will not sustainably sell below marginal cost) -- the SAME one-sided shape as ROUND 30's kinetics bound but a WEAKER foundation than R30's physical law; the named exception (predatory cross-subsidy) is this episode's own theme and is carried aloud, NOT excluded.
theorem_2_historical_undercut.attribution_caveat: Dow specifically only under a LABELLED assumption (he was a leading continuing US brine-bromine producer 1904-1908; the sources do NOT disclose his own price or cost). The claim is stated at the route/industry level.
theorem_2_historical_undercut.not_used_as_cost: The German dumping floor (15/12/10.5 c/lb) is the CARTEL's aggressor price, presented as the price-war trajectory only. Dow's 27 c/lb re-export is ARBITRAGE (buy German @15, resell Europe), a spread not a production-cost datum. Neither is used to bound Dow's cost.

historical_secondary.family: business-history narrative (SECONDARY, cross-corroborated across independent outlets)

sources.cite: Folsom, Burton W. Jr., 'Herbert Dow and Predatory Pricing', FEE
Mackinac Center, 'Herbert Dow, the Monopoly Breaker' (V1997-13)

historical_primary_usgs.family: USGS Data Series 140, bromine historical statistics (PRIMARY; same source family as the R16 USGS bromine price)
historical_primary_usgs.ton_basis: METRIC TONNE -- file header row A3: '[All values are in metric tons (t) bromine content unless otherwise noted]'. Conversion 1 t = 2204.6226 lb. (A short-ton misread would shift every c/lb figure ~10%.)
historical_primary_usgs.read_method: urllib HTTP 200; xlsx parsed via stdlib zipfile+ElementTree (no openpyxl); sheet1 rows 6-16 = years 1900-1910

two_bearings.diversity: provenance-diverse: a narrative transaction price (secondary) vs a computed statistical unit value (USGS revenue/tonnage). NOT the reframed-check disease (not one quantity in two costumes).
two_bearings.what_the_agreement_buys: The close ~1 c/lb agreement holds ONLY at the war-clearing years (USGS 1905 15.01 vs secondary 15; USGS 1908 9.98 vs 10.5) -- and there it is largely COMMON-MODE, because during the war the US revenue/tonnage unit value IS the depressed clearing price the cartel dumped at (one market number read twice, not two independent bearings; evil-morty F2). At the UNDISTORTED pre-war point (1904) the families DISAGREE by ~20% (USGS 29.98 vs secondary 36), so both pre-war undercuts (0.3881 and 0.2653) are reported side by side, never merged into a single 'corroborated' figure. Even where the price levels agree, it does NOT touch the price->cost upper-bound step (that rests on the economic premise), so no confidence is laundered from the price to Dow's cost.
two_bearings.independence_boundary: Full independence-to-root is NOT proven -- at the war years the agreement is common-mode by construction (the depressed clearing price), and both families could ultimately draw on the same period trade-journal price reporting. Asserted-diverse, not established-independent.

results.method: inflation-neutral ratios of same-era prices; one-sided ECONOMIC lower bounds at the route/industry level
